title: Start here
text:
Listen · Decode · Analyze · Share  
 Welcome aboard! This wiki helps you install SDRCC, connect your receivers and get from a quiet dashboard to ships, aircraft, radio traffic and satellite reception. 
 🧭 Start here 
 
 
 
 Guide 
 What you will do 
 
 
 
 
  Installation  
 Install SDRCC on Ubuntu and open the dashboard 
 
 
  First steps  
 Set up receiver bindings and check your station 
 
 
  Marine and ATIS  
 Listen to marine traffic, match vessels and replay recordings 
 
 
  Radio and aircraft  
 Use the Radio Receiver, Airband and ADS-B 
 
 
  Satellite missions  
 Plan passes and find reception results 
 
 
  Android app  
 Connect your phone, configure map plugins and update the app 
 
 
  Updates and troubleshooting  
 Update SDRCC and investigate common problems 
 
 
 
  New installation?  Follow Installation → First steps → the reception guide you need. 
 🖥️ One station, several views 
 SDRCC runs on your Ubuntu computer. The desktop dashboard provides configuration, receiver management and mission planning. The optional Android companion connects to that same station for viewing, listening and selected controls. 
   
 💬 Help shape the project 
 Found a bug? Include your version, what you expected, what happened and the steps to reproduce it. Have an idea? Explain what it would help you do at your station. 
  Discussions  ·  Issues  ·  Project README  
 
 These guides describe the stable SDRCC v0.67.0 / Android v2.0.0 user interface and use the project screenshots from 14 October 2026. Development changes are tested on develop before reaching main.

title: Installation
text:
Before you start 
 Use an  Ubuntu Linux x86-64 computer  with an internet connection for installation. Ubuntu Desktop is the main development and test environment; Ubuntu Server can also be used with a remote browser. The full SDRCC workload is intended for an x86-64 PC. Raspberry Pi is not the reference platform for this project. 
 Connect suitable RTL-SDR receivers and antennas for the signals you want to receive. Hardware bindings can also be configured after installation. 
 1. Open Terminal 
 For a fresh installation, run: 
  sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y git
git clone --depth 1 --branch main https://github.com/EyeVisionsNL/SDRCC.git ~/SDRCC
cd ~/SDRCC
./install.sh
  
 Run  ./install.sh as your normal Ubuntu user . The installer requests elevated privileges when needed. 
 2. Complete the installer 
 Enter the station name, location, latitude, longitude and altitude when asked. Use your own station values: satellite pass calculations depend on them. Follow the AIS-catcher setup prompts, or defer receiver configuration until the hardware is connected. 
 3. Open the dashboard 
 On the SDRCC computer, open  http://localhost:8080 . From another computer on the same trusted network, replace localhost with the SDRCC computer's IP address, for example  http://192.168.1.50:8080 . This address is an example. 
 Open  System  and continue with  First steps . 
   
 Set up AIS later 
 Stop active missions and Radio Receiver sessions, then run: 
  cd ~/SDRCC
./install.sh --ais-setup
  
 Already installed? 
 Use  System → Advanced Maintenance  for managed updates. See  Updates and troubleshooting . 
  Home  · Next:  First steps

title: First steps
text:
1. Check System 
 Open  System  and check service status and detected receiver hardware. A configured slot is a logical role; it does not mean a particular USB socket. 
 2. Bind the receivers 
 Under  System → Receiver hardware + bindings , assign the detected receiver serials to  SDR1 / SDR2 . Use  None  for an unused slot. Check the physical serial before assigning a receiver: USB indexes can change after reconnecting or restarting. 
   
 3. Check the role assignments 
 Open  Radio Control  to inspect receiver assignments and RF settings. Decide which receiver should provide AIS, ADS-B or a temporary listening task. A receiver already doing another job may need to be handed over by Receiver Manager. 
   
 4. Test one task first 
 Start the reception service you want to test and confirm its status. For Marine listening, continue with  Marine and ATIS . For aircraft or general listening, use  Radio and aircraft . Once one task works, add the next service and check that its receiver is available. 
 5. Allow browser audio 
 Start listening using the page's audio controls. If the browser blocks playback, allow audio for the SDRCC site and check the tab and system volume. A running receiver and audible browser playback are separate checks. 
 Know where to look 
 
 
 
 Page 
 Purpose 
 
 
 
 
 System 
 Health, hardware, bindings and maintenance 
 
 
 Radio Control 
 Assignments, receiver status and RF settings 
 
 
 Radio View 
 Aircraft, vessels and satellite overview 
 
 
 Traffic Voice 
 Marine or Airband listening and correlations 
 
 
 Radio Receiver 
 Direct tuning, spectrum and waterfall 
 
 
 Mission Planner / Control 
 Pass planning and scheduled reception 
 
 
 Mission Operations / History / Analytics 
 Results and reception quality 
 
 
 Logs 
 Details when a task does not work as expected

title: Marine & ATIS
text:
1. Open Traffic Voice 
 Choose  Marine Voice + AIS . Check the receiver assignment and select the marine channels you want to hear. Use a fixed channel to test reception, then enable scanning if you want to follow several channels. 
   
 2. Adjust reception 
 Use  Smart Gain  or select manual gain, then adjust squelch to keep background noise closed while allowing wanted transmissions through. Compare changes on the same channel. More gain is not always better: strong local signals can overload the receiver. 
 The selectable Marine channel filter and speech/noise reduction controls help tailor listening. Audio processing preferences are separate for Marine and Airband; the ATIS decoding input remains unchanged by speech noise reduction. 
 Channel lists support Excel import/export. Check an imported list before scanning and exclude channels you do not want to monitor. AIS data channels are not voice-listening channels. 
 3. Understand Possible Speaker 
 SDRCC decodes marine  ATIS — Automatic Transmitter Identification System  and correlates validated identities with available AIS vessel information.  Possible Speaker  shows a candidate vessel and matching information when a correlation is available. 
 A clear voice transmission does not guarantee a valid ATIS decode or an AIS match. The transmitting station may not supply a usable ATIS burst, reception may be incomplete, or the necessary AIS identity information may be unavailable. Treat the result as correlation information. 
   
 4. Replay or save a transmission 
 Use the recent Marine recordings to replay up to the four latest receptions. Save a recording you want to keep while live reception continues. Check the displayed channel when comparing transmissions. 
 5. Use the map and photographs 
 The desktop  Auto  function can follow validated matches in the AIS-catcher map, reusing the map window and retaining its zoom. On Android, a match highlights the vessel without re-centering the map; tap it yourself for details. 
 Optional  Ship photos  shows a vessel thumbnail with photographer credit and a link to the original page. Click the credit/source link to view the original. Existing watermarks remain intact.  Google Images  is a separate search link. 
 The VTS Rijnmond sector overlay is a separate project. On maps with the plugins installed, enable  VTS sector  and  SDRCC ATIS  in the map's plugin selector.

title: Radio & aircraft
text:
Radio Receiver: tune directly 
 
 Open  Radio Receiver  and check that a receiver can be allocated. 
 Select a preset or enter the wanted frequency. 
 Select the appropriate demodulation mode. SDRCC supports  LSB, USB, CW, AM, NFM, FM and WFM . 
 Start reception and enable audio playback. 
 Use the spectrum/waterfall and click-to-tune controls to inspect the signal. Adjust tuning steps, gain and RF-power squelch as needed. 
 Stop the Radio Receiver when finished so Receiver Manager can release it and restore its previous role. 
 
   
 Airband Voice and ADS-B 
 Open  Traffic Voice  and select  Airband Voice + ADS-B  for aviation listening. Choose the channels to scan or listen on a fixed channel. Airband audio preferences are separate from Marine settings. 
 ADS-B provides aircraft data; Airband Voice provides radio audio. Check both reception paths independently when one works and the other does not. Use  Radio View  for the combined overview and the aircraft map for aircraft details. 
   
 If a receiver is busy 
 Check  Radio Control , Traffic Voice, Radio Receiver and active missions. Receiver Manager coordinates access to a physical dongle: multiple logical roles do not create extra receivers. Stop the task you no longer need through its normal controls, then retry. 
  Home  ·  First steps  ·  Updates and troubleshooting

title: Satellite missions
text:
1. Check the station 
 Confirm that your station location and receiver bindings are correct. Connect an antenna suitable for the satellite signal. A predicted pass alone does not guarantee reception: the satellite must be transmitting the wanted mode and your station must be able to receive it. 
 2. Open Mission Planner 
 Review upcoming passes and the reception rules for the satellite you want to receive. Check timing, receiver availability and the configured reception settings before scheduling. 
   
 For an announced event such as ISS SSTV, check the current event announcement and its frequency, mode and active dates. Event times can change; an old announcement is not evidence that a transmission is currently active. 
 3. Watch Mission Control 
 Use  Mission Control  to inspect the upcoming queue, assigned receiver and scheduler state. At reception time SDRCC reserves the required receiver and handles conflicting receiver services. After the pass, it releases the receiver and can restore its earlier context. 
   
 4. Open the received products 
 Use  Mission Operations  to view the products associated with a mission.  Mission History  keeps previous results;  Mission Analytics  provides reception information such as Peak SNR and receiver performance. 
   
 Automated METEOR-M2 3 / METEOR-M2 4 LRPT reception uses SatDump. ISS Voice provides pass planning and reception. Check the available mission type and configuration on your installed version. 
 When a pass produces no usable result 
 Check the mission status and logs first. Compare the planned and actual reception window, receiver assignment, antenna, gain, satellite activity and available reception-quality information. A completed recording can still contain a weak or absent signal. 
 On Android you can view upcoming missions and selected scheduling controls. Create and configure missions in the main desktop dashboard.

title: Android app
text:
SDRCC Mobile connects to the SDRCC computer already running your receivers. The computer stays switched on; the phone provides remote viewing, listening and selected controls. 
 1. Install the official app 
 
 Use  Android 8.0 or later . 
 Download the  official signed SDRCC Mobile v2.0.0 APK . 
 Open the download. Allow installation from your browser if Android asks, then tap  Install . 
 Open SDRCC Mobile. Enter your SDRCC computer's address, such as  192.168.1.50:8080  (example), and tap  Verbinden met SDRCC . 
 
 Use the same trusted Wi-Fi network as the computer, or a private Tailscale connection. To correct a saved address, choose  IP-adres wijzigen , then  Adres bewerken  or  Wissen . 
   
 2. Enable the AIS map plugins 
 
 Open  Marine . 
 Start Marine Voice and/or AIS as needed; they have independent controls. 
 Open the AIS map's  plugin selector . 
 Enable  VTS sector  and  SDRCC ATIS , where installed. 
 A validated ATIS/AIS match highlights the vessel. Tap it for details: the map does not automatically move or re-center. 
 
       
 3. Check map connections 
 Open  System → Settings → Map Connections . If all services run on the same computer with standard ports, use: 
 
 
 
 Connection 
 Example 
 
 
 
 
 SDRCC 
 http://192.168.1.50:8080 
 
 
 AIS-Catcher Map URL 
 http://192.168.1.50:8119/ 
 
 
 ADS-B Map URL 
 http://192.168.1.50/tar1090/ 
 
 
 
 Replace the example IP with your own computer's reachable address. If a map runs on a different computer, use that computer's address. Choose  Save Map Addresses . 
 4. Connect away from home 
 Connect the SDRCC computer and Android phone to the same private Tailscale network. In SDRCC Mobile, use the  computer's Tailscale IP , not the phone's IP. Change map addresses to reachable Tailscale addresses too if required. 
 Keep Tailscale connected on both devices. Test using mobile data with Wi-Fi switched off. The  detailed Android and Tailscale guide  contains the full setup steps. No public router port forwarding is needed for this setup. 
 5. Replay recordings and use the other tabs 
 Replay or save recent Marine recordings while live reception continues. The aircraft tab provides ADS-B controls and the aircraft map. Satellite pages show positions, upcoming missions and received images, with selected mission controls. System shows service status and usage. 
     
 6. Update the Android app 
 Tap  ↓  in the top toolbar, or  App-update controleren  on the connection screen. If a newer signed version is available, choose  APK openen , download it and select  Update / Bijwerken . Install over the existing signed app to retain settings. 
 Use official signed release APKs. Historical debug builds can have incompatible signing keys. 
  The Android button updates only the phone app.  Update the SDRCC computer through  System → Advanced Maintenance  in the desktop dashboard. Receiver bindings, full mission planning and detailed history/analytics also remain in the desktop interface.

title: Updates & help
text:
Update SDRCC 
 
 Open the desktop dashboard and go to  System → Advanced Maintenance . 
 Check the offered version and release notes. Use the stable main channel for the stable release; develop contains changes under test. 
 Finish active reception work that should not be interrupted, then start the managed update. 
 Wait for the update result. Reopen or refresh the dashboard and check the installed version and service status. 
 
 The managed workflow preserves local station settings, receiver bindings and runtime data outside the code replacement path. 
   
 Find the right first check 
 
 
 
 Symptom 
 What to check 
 
 
 
 
 Dashboard will not open 
 Computer powered on, SDRCC running, correct IP and port, reachable network 
 
 
 Receiver is missing 
 USB connection, detected serial and System receiver bindings 
 
 
 Receiver is busy 
 Active mission, Traffic Voice or Radio Receiver ownership in the dashboard 
 
 
 Receiver runs but there is no audio 
 Page playback control, browser audio permission, muted tab/system output and squelch 
 
 
 Voice is audible but no vessel match 
 Validated ATIS decode and available AIS vessel identity data; not every transmission yields a match 
 
 
 Android connects but maps do not 
 Each map URL under System → Settings → Map Connections, relevant map service and reachability 
 
 
 Sector or ATIS overlay is missing 
 Installed map plugins and selection of VTS sector / SDRCC ATIS 
 
 
 Works on Wi-Fi but not remotely 
 Tailscale connected on both devices; computer's Tailscale address used for station and maps 
 
 
 Satellite mission has no usable image/audio 
 Mission logs, actual reception window, receiver, antenna, gain and satellite transmission activity 
 
 
 
 An update failed 
 Copy the exact error and check the update log. For  Update source hash is not approved , report the named file, current version and update channel so the release metadata can be checked. Do not edit hashes or disable verification as a workaround. 
 If a receiver or mission is reported as active, inspect Mission Control and the listening pages before retrying. Stop an active task through its normal controls. If the warning remains despite an idle station, include that in the report. 
 Make a useful bug report 
 Include: 
 
 SDRCC version and branch/channel; Android version if relevant. 
 Ubuntu version and receiver model, plus the affected service. 
 The steps to reproduce the problem. 
 Expected result and actual result. 
 Exact error, relevant log excerpt and a screenshot where useful. 
 
 Remove passwords, tokens and other private information from shared logs or screenshots. 
   
  Report a bug  ·  Questions and future ideas  
 Remove SDRCC 
 If you intend to uninstall, run  ~/SDRCC/uninstall.sh  and read its prompts carefully. The receipt-aware uninstaller removes externally provisioned radio applications only when the installation receipt records that SDRCC installed them. Shared Ubuntu packages are preserved.
